images.title: James Keauiluna Kaulia
images.caption: James Keauiluna Kaulia, c. 1893. The newest source-locked reconstruction is shown first. The exact uploaded parent image and a separate archival reference remain available underneath; earlier attempts stay in the process archive instead of cluttering the public controls.
images.source_record_label: Library of Congress, Representative Committee of Delegates of the Hawaiian People, c. 1893; J.K. Kaulia identified in the group portrait
images.source_image_access_note: Public-domain crop of Kaulia from the archival group photograph; the Library of Congress catalog record remains source authority.
images.rights_note: Library of Congress lists no known restrictions on publication for the source group photograph; Wikimedia marks the crop public domain in the United States.
images.color_reason: Proof-of-concept reconstruction uses restrained period-plausible tones: warm brown skin, white shirt/cuffs, dark charcoal suit, muted brown-gray waistcoat, and a neutral studio background. Exact garment and backdrop colors are not recoverable from the albumen print and remain explicitly interpretive.
images.reconstruction_reason: The preferred presentation is a source-locked reconstruction of the uploaded portrait. Earlier derived attempts remain durable process evidence but no longer occupy public view controls.

images.title: ʻIolani Palace
images.caption: ʻIolani Palace around 1889–1890, several years before the September 1897 Palace Square meeting. The source-locked wide reconstruction leads, the separate close reconstruction adds a genuinely different view, and the exact uploaded source plus archive access copy remain underneath.
images.source_record_label: Hawaiʻi State Archives, PPWD-1-8-010, Buildings Government - Iolani Palace, c. 1890, Theodore P. Severin
images.source_image_access_note: Web access copy of a period exterior palace photograph; Hawaiʻi State Archives PPWD-1-8-010 anchors the c. 1890 place/date authority for this proving record.
images.rights_note: The archival source is a late-19th-century photograph. The project preserves source provenance and does not silently promote the web access copy into archival authority.
images.color_reason: The overall reconstruction is anchored by the surviving/restored palace's known light masonry, dark roof, tropical green grounds, and Honolulu sky. Exact 1889–1890 paint, vegetation, atmospheric, and material colors are still estimates.
images.reconstruction_reason: The newest wide view is the preferred source-locked reconstruction. The close view remains public because it materially changes the view; older near-duplicates are preserved only as process evidence.

images.title: Pounding poi - preparing dinner, Hawaiian Islands
images.caption: Pounding poi in Hawaiʻi, 1896. The reconstructed daily-life view leads for immediacy, with the original 1896 stereograph immediately available underneath. Color and restoration experiments remain in the process archive.
images.source_record_label: Library of Congress, Pounding poi - preparing dinner, Hawaiian Islands, 1896, LC-DIG-stereo-1s12133
images.source_image_access_note: Large JPEG digital file from the original stereograph, provided by the Library of Congress.
images.rights_note: Library of Congress lists no known restrictions on publication.
images.color_reason: The proof-of-concept reconstruction uses restrained brown earth/wood and skin tones, muted green vegetation, and neutral cloth. Exact clothing, vessel, vegetation, and food colors are not established by the stereograph and remain best estimates.
images.reconstruction_reason: Derived daily-life reconstruction. It should be read beside the original stereograph rather than as replacement source evidence. The contaminated Batch 003 poi attempt was intentionally not routed into the site.

feed_images.color_reason: No separate color-only state in this public stack.
feed_images.reconstruction_reason: Historically informed portrait reconstruction paired with a period identity reference. The newer reconstruction is preferred visually, but it remains a derived likeness rather than source authority.

feed_images.title: Honolulu Harbor
feed_images.caption: Honolulu Harbor in 1890, used as near-period context for shipping, arrivals, and naval pressure in the 1897 feed. The reconstruction leads for immediacy, with the archival harbor reference directly underneath.

feed_images.source_image_access_note: Public-domain Hawaiʻi State Archives harbor photograph available through Wikimedia Commons.
feed_images.rights_note: Wikimedia Commons marks the archival photograph public domain.

feed_images.reconstruction_reason: General steamship-era harbor reconstruction. Do not identify the generated ship as USS Bennington or treat generated signage as historical evidence. The 1890 harbor photograph remains a related place reference rather than the literal parent source.

feed_images.rights_note: Period archival photograph; source record is preserved explicitly.

feed_images.title: Anti-annexation organizing, Hilo
feed_images.caption: A Sept. 16, 1897 Hilo anti-annexation meeting survives visually as a newspaper illustration. The preferred photo reconstruction is shown first and the original newspaper image is one click away. Other reconstruction attempts remain in the process archive.
feed_images.source_record_label: The San Francisco Call, Sept. 30, 1897, illustration of the Sept. 16 anti-annexation meeting at Hilo
feed_images.source_image_access_note: Public-domain historical newspaper illustration of a documented 1897 anti-annexation meeting in Hilo.
feed_images.rights_note: Wikimedia Commons marks the historical newspaper image public domain in the United States.
feed_images.color_reason: Color, faces, materials, and fine detail in the photo reconstruction are interpretive because the parent source is an illustration.
feed_images.reconstruction_reason: Approved as a clearly labeled photo reconstruction from the documented Hilo newspaper illustration. The historical illustration owns event identity and broad composition; generated demographic appearance and anatomy were explicitly reviewed after several failed attempts.

photo_posts.feed_rendering:
Hilo, Sept. 16, 1897.
The anti-annexation movement was still filling rooms and raising hands. This scene survives as a newspaper illustration; the photo reconstruction follows that source.
photo_posts.relationship_note: Photo reconstruction derived from a documented Sept. 16 Hilo anti-annexation newspaper illustration. It is same-movement context, not a photograph of the Sept. 6 Palace Square meeting.
